issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either assume $\rho\in W^{1,\infty}(D_T)$ in the proposition and prove the $\chi_K$ remark by the locality property of H-convergence, or supply an additional argument (e.g. uniform Meyers higher integrability of $\nabla\phi^\varepsilon,\nabla\psi^\varepsilon$ giving weak $L^{p/2}$ compactness of the energy densities) that permits passing to the limit against $L^\infty$ weights.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative comparison $|A-B|\le C\rho(1-\rho)$ and its corollary are unproved for non-smooth (in particular indicator or time-dependent) transition functions, which is exactly the setting the paper advertises and uses numerically; the remark that $B=A$ for $\rho=\chi_K$ needs a separate (locality-of-H-convergence) argument.
issues.title: H-limit comparison proof tests the PDE with (1-ρ)φφ^ε, which requires regularity of ρ that is never assumed (and fails for ρ=χ_K)
issues.why_classification: The conclusion is plausibly true, but closing the gap needs a contained nontrivial argument (higher integrability/equi-integrability) or a hypothesis restriction that removes the advertised non-smooth ρ from the proposition; no global re-architecture is needed.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that $a^\varepsilon$ and $A_H$ (hence $b^\varepsilon_H$) are symmetric to Lemma lem:added-1 and Theorem thm:global (and drop the transposes), or supply a separate nonsymmetric stability argument.
issues.overall_effect: (sta2) and hence (sta4), (thm12) and (thm13) in Theorem thm:global — the advertised $H^1$ macroscopic estimate without $\Delta t^{-1/2}$ and the $\ell^2(L^2)$ estimate of $\partial_t u-\delta U$ used in Remark rmk:local — are established only for symmetric coefficients; (sta1) and (thm11) are unaffected.
issues.title: Energy stability (sta2) uses a symmetric-form identity for a possibly nonsymmetric coefficient
issues.why_classification: A symmetry assumption restores every estimate with the same rates, but it withdraws the nonsymmetric coefficients that the paper's setting explicitly includes; proving the nonsymmetric case would require substantially different tools.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds $\|\nabla(I-R_h)(\omega u_k^\varepsilon)\|_{L^2(K)}$ by the best approximation error of $\omega u_k^\varepsilon$ in $L^2(K)$ (whole hybrid region) and then simply rewrites this quantity with $L^2(K_0)$ in the final triangle inequality and in the statement (eq:3.6). The $L^2(K_0)$ infimum does not control $\|\nabla V\|_{L^2(K\backslash K_0)}$ for near-minimizers, so the stated inequality is not what the argument proves.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $L^2(K_0)$ by $L^2(K)$ in the first term of (eq:3.6) and in the last display of the proof.
issues.overall_effect: Estimate (eq:3.6) as stated is unsupported; the proved version has the approximation term over $K$, consistent with the introduction and Theorem thm:local.
issues.title: Theorem thm:localest1 states the best-approximation term over $K_0$ while the proof only controls it over $K$
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the statement to what the proof delivers preserves the method and rates; the only loss is the slightly stronger (unproved) localization of the approximation term.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State explicitly the assumption $u^\varepsilon\in C([0,T];W^{1,p}(K))$ (or sufficient data regularity, e.g. $f\in W^{1,p}(0,T;W^{-1,p})$ with compatible $u_0$, yielding it via Meyers for $\partial_t u^\varepsilon$) and remove the claim that it follows from Lemma lem:added-2 alone.
issues.overall_effect: The combined interior estimate displayed in the introduction and derived in Remark rmk:local rests on an unestablished hypothesis; the theorems themselves remain valid under their stated (but unjustified) $\ell^2(0,T;W^{1,p}(K))$ assumption, whose uniformity in $\varepsilon$ is not addressed.

issues.why_classification: Adding the correct time-regularity hypothesis is a local fix that keeps all theorems and rates; only the claim that Meyers' estimate alone suffices (no smoothness of $\partial_t u^\varepsilon$ needed) has to be withdrawn.
